quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the minimum amount of Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL) insurance that drivers must have?
questions.explanation: Florida law requires all drivers to have at least $10,000 in PIP insurance and $10,000 in PDL insurance. You must show proof of this insurance when you register your vehicle.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, when can you pass?

options.text: If you are on an expressway.

questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass. You can only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should a driver do when entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp?

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from a ramp, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when you have a clear opportunity.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires slide on water on the road. Low air pressure, bad tire tread, and speeding all increase the risk. Do all three to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Not turn on any vehicle lights.

questions.explanation: You must turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use your low beams when you see an oncoming vehicle or are following another car. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: The amount of food in the stomach
The body weight of an individual
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks. Food slows alcohol absorption but does not prevent intoxication.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your distance from the car ahead. Your vehicle needs more time to stop than it does on dry roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an overpass is coming with low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this example).

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a driving hazard ahead.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and emergency work ahead.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance in all these situations: behind large vehicles blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting highways, behind motorcycles or bicycles, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: What can you do from the center turn lane?
questions.explanation: This lane is for left turns only. You cannot use it to pass other cars or for through-traffic.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Speed up to match their speed.
Move right to let them pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let them pass and then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right to let them pass.
questions.explanation: On multilane highways, move to the right lane when it is safe to do so. The left lane is for faster vehicles to pass slower ones.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: You do not need to stop.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the divider ahead.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, you should:

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face two hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the wheel to force your vehicle back on the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Then gradually steer back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Then gradually steer back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the pavement and gently apply the brakes to slow down. When your speed is safe, turn the wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the wheel sharply.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on:

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side traffic is moving toward.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest you.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers they cannot park in this area.

questions.question: You notice a defect that could affect your vehicle's safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops the vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive the same as if they were thinking clearly.
Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions make it hard to focus on driving because your mind is on something else. Take time to calm down before you start driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers the road may be wet and slippery.

questions.question: Always use your signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, yield to the driver on your right. You may then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk. Stay alert at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow warning signs (orange in work areas). They warn you of a hazard ahead or an area with special rules.

questions.question: You see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to avoid hurting the pedestrian.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering from a driveway or private road, you must yield to traffic already on the public road. Merge safely when you can.

questions.question: When driving, you are allowed to text:

options.text: If you don't look at the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal. It is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: After an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop at or near the scene.
Turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes. Turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and turn off the ignition.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need extra effort to steer. Slow down and carefully drive to a safe spot to stop.

questions.question: You are angry after work. Before driving home, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you don't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Have drinks at a bar before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, cool off before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others.

questions.question: A green arrow becomes a solid green light. What does this mean?

options.text: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass another car going the same direction.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
Police will always give them a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What should you do if a gate at a drawbridge starts to lower?

options.text: Find another way around the gate.
Drive quickly under the lowering gate.
Stop completely and wait for the gate to go back up.
Stop only if you cannot fit under the gate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait for the gate to go back up.
questions.explanation: Drawbridges have flashing red lights and bells. Stop when the lights flash before the gate lowers. Driving around or under the gate is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect stopping ability. Slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition to keep control and stop safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit on wet roads, when visibility is poor, or when conditions are not ideal. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions even if you are within the posted limit.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed on a road under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. You must drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when weather and road conditions are bad.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on one-way streets and ramps to tell you not to continue in your current direction.

questions.question: How should you enter a highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to avoid other cars.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to highway speed. Signal, find an opening, match the traffic speed, and merge safely.
